title: Pressure sensor calibration drift after power supply fluctuation
description: Three pressure sensors in the cleanroom monitoring system reported readings 15-20% below expected values. The deviation appeared suddenly following a brief power fluctuation event (UPS switchover lasting 200ms). Sensors did not return to normal after power stabilized. Other sensor types on the same power circuit were unaffected.
root_cause: The pressure sensors use a piezoelectric transducer that requires a stable reference voltage for accurate measurements. The 200ms power interruption during UPS switchover caused the internal reference capacitor to partially discharge. When power returned, the reference voltage settled at a lower-than-specified level, introducing a systematic negative offset to all readings. This is a known sensitivity in sensors using the MPX5700 series transducer.
resolution_steps: Compare affected sensor readings against a portable calibrated reference gauge
Power cycle affected sensors with a minimum 30-second off period to fully discharge and reset the reference capacitor
Verify readings return to expected range after power cycle
If readings remain offset, perform factory recalibration procedure via serial interface
Install power conditioning filters on the sensor supply rail to suppress transients below 500ms
Add UPS transfer time monitoring to correlate future pressure anomalies with power events
